proposal.summary: R2 covers CM550's high speed governor (HSG) and all speed governor (ASG) data. The HSG code (runHighSpeedGovernorPid, presetHighSpeedGovernorIntegrator, initializeHighSpeedGovernorGainSet, selectHighSpeedGovernorGainSet, selectEngineSpeedLimit, initializeEngineSpeedLimitDefaults, all already twins with CM848) reads e2m blocks 1060 / 1061 / 1062 / 1063 / 1290 / 128F / 13AB / 13B4 / 109C. These blocks hold the same records as CM848's. The ASG (cm550_runAllSpeedGovernor and its mode selectors, counterparts of cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor and cm848_selectAllSpeedGovernorApplicationMode) uses blocks 107A / 107C / 1170 with the same mnemonics, so 89 of the 100 rows take CM848's names. The code settled two e2m layout quirks. First, CM550's 107C records past +0x1F (the QPID terms) overlap block 107A, so 0x80a992 / 0x80a996 / 0x80a99a are droop gain 1 / throttle droop gain 1 / the selected droop. Second, CM550 has extra words in 1060 (+0x20), 1062 (+2 / +4) and 107A (+2), so the later records sit 2 to 4 bytes after CM848's. The 11 rows without a CM848 row took names from their code or their record. Retyped: 0x800716 to i32 (an integer integrator whose low word is the integral term), 0x80a996 and 0x80a942 to word, 0x80d652 to i16. Added 24 unnamed DAT_ words of the same blocks and the CM848 counterpart of 0x800182.

globals.comment: The high speed governor integrator (no e2m record), a 32-bit fuel count. runHighSpeedGovernorPid adds error x adjusted integral gain / 0x3c00, subtracts the proportional gain change term, and clamps it between high_speed_governor_integrator_minimum and _maximum with signed long compares. Outside fueling state 12, presetHighSpeedGovernorIntegrator sets it to final_fueling minus the positive proportional term plus at most high_speed_governor_integrator_preset_offset_limit, clamped to the preset limits. high_speed_governor_integral_term (0x80d62c) is its low word (dump 0x0000019b = 411 = the term). This differs from CM848's Q16.16 high_speed_governor_integrator (0x3fa890), whose high word is the term. Only the overspeed reset path writes the reset value into the high word and clears the low word. (was hsg_integrator_fuel_output, type undefined; PR #53 round 97)

Notes and scratch scripts are in /home/linux/.claude/jobs/374b0424/tmp/w15/r97/scratch/R2/describer/ (notes.md, dis_*.txt, users.txt, absrefs.txt, dump_values.txt). All 100 rows are RAM or extended RAM, outside the EEPROM mirror, so no name takes _cal.
- Match records by mnemonic, not by offset. CM550's blocks have extra words: 1060 +20 HSPZGVEN, 1062 +2 / +4 blank spots, 107A +2 ASRFST.
- v64t6_s.e2m resolves 107C +1A..+2E (the 4-byte QPID records) into 107A. In this firmware 107C ends at 0x80a983: 0x80a984 is the reference filter state and 107A starts at 0x80a98c. The code settles 0x80a992 / 0x80a996 / 0x80a99a as ASDPGN01 / ASTH01DP / ASSLDP.
- Misnamed user functions (out of scope; the evidence is in notes.md):
  - 0xd0e2 cm550_diagnosticDataCopyHandler is the ASG application mode selection (counterpart cm848_selectAllSpeedGovernorApplicationMode).
  - 0xd3e6 cm550_diagnosticMode10FuelController is the droop / droop gain calculation (counterpart cm848_calculateGovernorCompensatorCoefficients).
  - 0xd2be cm550_acceleratorThrottleFaultDetector does the tuning set selection and the throttle reference.
  - 0xd218 and 0xd584 are the TSC1 (state 2) and throttle (state 7) reference claims.
  - 0xd1a4 is the TSC1 speed control mode entry.
  - 0xc8a0 cm550_dzgTimingAndPressureControlStateMachine is the ASG reference rate limit and blend (counterpart cm848_calculateGovernorReferenceSpeedBlend).
  - 0xd23c cm550_dualTableLookupSum is the ASG no-load fuel (counterpart cm848_calculateAllSpeedGovernorNoLoadFuel).
  - 0xfb26 vp44_fuelLimitExceedanceStatisticsAccumulator is the J1939 torque curve builder (counterpart cm848_updateJ1939EngineConfigurationTorqueCurve).
  - 0xfaa6 is the points 2 / 5 droop helper (counterpart cm848_setJ1939TorqueCurvePoints2And5AtDroopLineFueling).
- Code that is not in the dump: the HSG lead / lag compensator (nothing dumped writes 0x80d60a) and the working gain set writer (0x80d610-0x80d618 have no writer). Candidates are the undumped calls around the HSG task (func_0x00044c76 / func_0x0004da56 before the PID, func_0x00042496 after it).
- Difference in the twin selectHighSpeedGovernorGainSet: with gain scheduling disabled, CM550 does nothing, while CM848 loads the base set and code 16.
- The CM550 HSG integrator 0x800716 holds whole counts (integral term = low word). CM848's is Q16.

verdict.overall: I checked 125 global rows: the 100 family rows, the 24 new DAT_ rows and the CM848 counterpart row 0x3fa8a4. The batch proposed no functions, prototypes or enum members. The investigator's skipped[] is empty and should stay empty: the code or the e2m record settles every row. The rows that rest on their record are the 13B4 / 13AB +4 compensator words (not referenced in the dumped ROM; CM848 has the same block, offset and record), the two SWHSG blank words and HSGVSPOF 0x808506. I disassembled these functions myself and they confirm every proposed role: runHighSpeedGovernorPid, presetHighSpeedGovernorIntegrator, initializeHighSpeedGovernorGainSet, selectHighSpeedGovernorGainSet, selectEngineSpeedLimit, initializeEngineSpeedLimitDefaults, cm550_runAllSpeedGovernor, 0xc8a0, 0xd0e2-0xd5a0, 0xf716, 0xfaa6, 0xfb26 and the switch merges at 0x15248 / 0x15cde. Each reused CM848 name sits on the same e2m record. I matched records by mnemonic, because CM550's blocks 1060, 1062 and 107A have extra words. The CM848 bodies of the shared functions and of cm848_runOperatingModeSpeedGovernor run the same steps with the same constants. All names are unique in their firmware: I re-ran check_proposals.py and grepped against function and struct names. The new rows split or swallow no existing row (I checked the neighbouring struct sizes). All dump values in the comments match the RAM dump. Types confirmed: 0x800716 i32 (signed long clamps), 0x80a996 and 0x80a942 word, 0x80d652 i16 (signed tst.w + ble). 0x80d62c stays word: the PID sum reads it with ext.l, selectEngineSpeedLimit with unsigned cmp.w, and round 94 chose word. I amended two comments. 0x800182 cited its CM848 counterpart by the old name that this batch replaces. 0x80a9a2 said 'toggles'. The code writes the opposite of the default while the switch is on and the default while it is off, and only when the default is below 2, the throttle is 0 and final_fueling is below no-load + offset. Otherwise it keeps the value. Where the describer differed, the investigator's choice holds. 0x800182 is a 'derate' speed (JCT0P5IN calls it DERATE_SPEED). The spare words are _0 / _1 (SWHSG_00 / _01). 0x808506 and 0x80a9a2 keep the investigator's names. 0x80d644 / 0x80d646 / 0x808120 / 0x80812a / 0x808132 stay flat rows, because CM550 has neither struct type. Follow-ups, not applied: (1) add engine_speed_limit_arbitration_t at 0x80d644 (it would absorb 0x80d648 of another family) and high_speed_governor_gain_set_t at 0x80811e / 0x808128 / 0x808130. (2) Old names are mentioned in these places: the 28 CM550 global rows and 3 plate comments (0xd3b2 / 0x1ce7c / 0x1d5a0) that the investigator listed. Also CM848 rows 0x5c356 and 0x5c358 and the plate of cm848_setJ1939TorqueCurvePoints2And5AtDroopLineFueling 0x20c64 (torque_limit_working_reference), and the short forms asg_error_difference / asg_feedback_difference_term / asg_droop_gain_2 in the CM550 all_speed_governor_gain_set_t field comments. (3) The function leads are real misnames: 0xd0e2, 0xd3e6, 0xc8a0, 0xd23c, 0xd1a4, 0xd218, 0xd584, 0xd2be, 0xfb26, 0xfaa6. (4) Verified: with gain scheduling disabled, CM550 selectHighSpeedGovernorGainSet returns at once, while CM848 copies the base set. The twin differs in that one branch.

verdicts.final_comment: The engine speed that the J1939 engine configuration torque curve (PGN 65251) is derated to (no e2m record). vp44_fuelLimitExceedanceStatisticsAccumulator (0xfb26, the torque curve builder) sets it to 0x80d648 (HSRFBEDP) when engine_speed_limit_limiting_source_number is 1 / 2 / 4 / 5, otherwise to engine_speed_limit_reference. It compares it with JCT0P5IN 0x808174 'WHEN DERATE_SPEED < THIS POINT, LOW HP HSG REF. LINE LEFT' to select the point 4 or the point 5 fueling. cm550_calculateGovernorDroopSpeed makes it the point 2 speed when engine_speed_limit_droop_slope is 0. 20240 (2530 rpm) in the dump. CM848 counterpart: j1939_torque_curve_derate_engine_speed (0x3fa8a4, was torque_limit_working_reference), with the same two users. (was hsg_reference_speed_for_droop; PR #53 round 97)
verdicts.reason: Name and type confirmed. The only writer is 0xfb26: 0xfc04 stores 0x80d648 after cmpi.w #2/#4/#5/#1 of 0x80d644, 0xfc10 stores 0x80d64e. The reads are cmp.w with 0x808174 + bcc at 0xfcb0 / 0xfda0, which picks point 4 or point 5 fueling for 0xfaa6, and 0xfac2, which makes it the point 2 speed when the slope is 0. All 5 accesses are word. The record JCT0P5IN calls this value DERATE_SPEED, so 'derate' fits better than the describer's 'breakpoint'. Comment amended only because it named the CM848 counterpart by the old name that this batch replaces.

a3 = #0x800716 in runHighSpeedGovernorPid. The low word (2,a3) goes to 0x80d62c. presetHighSpeedGovernorIntegrator writes it with move.l (a2) and add.l. Only the reset path writes the HIGH word (0x1cf76) and clears 0x800718. The dump holds 0x0000019b = the integral term, so it is a whole-count 32-bit signed integrator. i32 is right, and the name matches the CM848 role.

verdicts.final_comment: e2m 107A +16 ASDPFG 'ASG DROOP SELECTION FLAG; USED TO SELECT DROOP SOURCE' (1 in the dump). It selects which of the two ASG tuning sets is used. Value 0: the reference speeds through all_speed_governor_minimum / maximum_reference_speed_1_pointer, and all_speed_governor_alternate_droop_lookup. Value 1: the _2 reference speeds and all_speed_governor_droop_lookup. cm550_initializeAllSpeedGovernorReferenceSpeedSets starts it from 0x803d5a (e2m 1387 +8 ASDPFGTN 'TRIM FOR ASG DROOP SELECTION FLAG'). cm550_acceleratorThrottleFaultDetector (0xd2be) writes it again only while 0x803d5a is below 2, the commanded throttle is 0 and final_fueling is below no_load_fuel_quantity + all_speed_governor_switch_droop_fueling_offset: the opposite of 0x803d5a while the STCG / ASG droop switch (bit 1 of 0x80bcd1) is on and algorithm_enable_flags_27_cal.switched_throttle_control_governor_select is 0, otherwise 0x803d5a. At other times it keeps its value. CM848's ASDPFG is a 0..128 blend weight in block 158D (all_speed_governor_tuning_set_blend_weight), so this row gets its own name. (was asg_throttle_source_selector; PR #53 round 97)
verdicts.reason: Name and type confirmed. In 0xd2be, 0 loads the set 1 pointers 0x80a9ac / 0x80a9b0 and 1 loads the set 2 pointers 0x80a9b4 / 0x80a9b8 into 0x80a9a4 / 0x80a9a6. In 0xd3e6, 1 selects lookup 0x800144 and 0 selects 0x800136. Initialized from 0x803d5a at 0xd3da. 'select' and 'selection' both have precedent, so the investigator's spelling stands. Comment amended: 'toggles it' was imprecise. 0xd306-0xd340 writes NOT(default) while the switch is on and the default while it is off (the default only when flags 27 bit 3 is set), and only under the default < 2 / no-load / zero-throttle gate. Otherwise the value is kept.

The only store is sth at 0x20e14 in cm848_updateJ1939EngineConfigurationTorqueCurve. It holds engine_speed_limit_reference, or engine_speed_limit_arbitrated for sources 1 / 2 / 4 / 5 / 12. It is a speed, not a torque limit, so the old name was wrong. The new name is unique in CM848. Word type is right.
